claim: Jacobs manages O&M of nine advanced treatment trains at West Basin's Edward C. Little Water Recycling Facility
The Edward C. Little Water Recycling Facility delivers five distinct grades of fit-for-purpose recycled water
Jacobs optimizes advanced RO, crystallizers, and exchangers to support the Turlock Irrigation District combined cycle power plant
Jacobs has provided long-term operations of the City of Clovis Water Reuse Facility since 2009
Jacobs has provided planning through O&M for the Clovis WWTP/WRF since 2009
Jacobs saved the City of Clovis more than $100,000 through value engineering on the Clovis WWTP/WRF
The Clovis WWTP/WRF is a 2.8-MGD facility
The Clovis WWTP serves as a scalping plant treating up to 2.8 MGD, with flow above that amount going to the Fresno-Clovis Regional WWTP
Since commencing operations in 2009 the Clovis WWTP/WRF has reliably and consistently met all State of California NPDES and water reclamation regulatory requirements

Clovis WWTP/WRF won the 2009 Design-Build Institute of America Excellence Award for Projects over $15 Million
Clovis WWTP/WRF won the 2009 Award of Merit from the WateReuse Association
Clovis WWTP/WRF was a 2009 Global Water Intelligence Water Reuse Project of the Year Finalist
Clovis WWTP/WRF won the 2009 American Academy of Environmental Engineers Design Honor Award for Excellence
Clovis WWTP/WRF won the 2008 Environmental Business Journal Wastewater Project Merit Award
Jacobs supported design, construction, start-up, and commissioning of Soquel Creek's advanced water treatment facility and now leads long-term operations
Following acceptance testing of the design-build facility, Jacobs began operating and maintaining the Soquel Creek facility for an initial term

Jacobs provides O&M support for the Turlock Irrigation District Zero Liquid Discharge Facility
The Turlock Zero Liquid Discharge Facility serves Turlock Irrigation District's combined cycle power plant
Jacobs Turlock Irrigation District contract dates
Turlock Zero Liquid Discharge Facility plant size, maximum monthly average
Jacobs staff developed WAC rinse procedures at Turlock that use one-fifth of the water and take less time than the old procedures required
Jacobs increased Turlock mixed beds throughput to exhaustion from 480,000 gallons to 500,000 gallons
The Turlock mixed beds throughput increase was a four percent increase without loss of quality
A new Jacobs cleaning method for RO equipment at Turlock using bulk chemicals in place of special-order RO cleaning chemicals generates chemical savings for the client annually
Jacobs has partnered with Turlock Irrigation District for almost 20 years
West Basin Municipal Water District awarded Jacobs an O&M services contract for the nation's largest advanced water reuse treatment facility
The Edward C. Little Water Recycling Facility produces five distinct grades of custom water through nine complex treatment streams
The Edward C. Little Water Recycling Facility is the only treatment facility to exist that produces five different types of fit-for-purpose recycled water
ECLWRF recycled water conserves enough drinking water to meet the needs of up to 80,000 households for a year

Jacobs also provides O&M services for four West Basin satellite facilities: Chevron Nitrification Treatment Plant, Juanita Millender-McDonald Carson Regional Water Recycling Plant, Torrance Refinery Water Recycling Plant, and Hyperion Effluent Pump Station
The West Basin facilities serve nearly 600 connections to municipal, industrial, and commercial businesses
